chunk_findings.detail: In `answered`, line 52 does `got = set(AN.answers(h))`, but line 57 then indexes that result with `got[f]`. `_unanswered` already assumes `AN.answers(h)` is a mapping from feature to status; converting it to a set produces a set of keys (or answer objects), not a subscriptable mapping. Therefore, for any tier with at least one required row, `answered(h, tier)` raises `TypeError: 'set' object is not subscriptable` instead of returning the answered features. This breaks the answered API and any test or report path that calls `gate.answered`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/gate.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The added `parity_gaps` array is not valid JSON: the openhands region contains the line `"openhands:stream-mapping",openhands:usage-and-cost",`, where the second value is not a JSON string because it lacks its opening quote and is not separated as a distinct array element. Any strict JSON loader used by `tests/harness_conformance/report.py` or `tests/test_parity_gate.py` will raise `JSONDecodeError` when reading this fixture (at the bare `openhands` token), so the conformance report/tests cannot load the gaps data.
chunk_findings.title: tests/harness_conformance/gaps.json (parity_gaps openhands entries)

chunk_findings.detail: Given a `gaps.json` that exists and is a dict but does not yet contain the new `parity_gaps` key (for example, the pre-change baseline `{"gaps": []}` or a baseline intentionally omitting the new key because there are no parity gaps), `parity_baseline()` raises `KeyError: 'parity_gaps'`. The function already treats a missing file or non-dict JSON as an empty baseline, so the new key should also be read as empty when absent (`data.get("parity_gaps", [])`); otherwise tools/tests that compare the current parity gap set to the committed baseline fail during migration or when the new key is omitted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/harness_conformance/report.py:parity_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: `answered` converts the answer mapping to a set (`got = set(AN.answers(h))`) but then indexes it (`got[f]`) at line 57 to test membership in `_ANSWERED`. Given any harness whose tier has at least one required feature, e.g. `AN.answers(h) == {"foo": "verified"}` and `required_features(tier) == ("foo",)`, the generator evaluates `got["foo"]` on a built-in `set`, raising `TypeError: 'set' object is not subscriptable`; the function cannot return answered features. It should inspect the mapping (`got.get(f) in _ANSWERED`) or keep `got = AN.answers(h)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/gate.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The new `parity_gaps` baseline is keyed only by `agent:feature`, but the stated rule and the test name make the tier part of the row identity: a descriptor is supported at a tier only when every row required for that tier is answered, and “a tier is a catalog axis and its required rows are its rows.” Collapsing the key to `agent:feature` makes distinct tier rows indistinguishable. For example, if `claude:steer` is already listed as a known gap for one tier, a newly added `claude:steer` row for another tier with no answers produces the same baseline key and therefore does not appear as a new gap, so the ratchet incorrectly allows the new unanswered tier row to pass. Conversely, if the gate emits tier-qualified gap keys, none of these 585 entries match the current gaps, so every existing gap is treated as new. Either way, this data cannot enforce the per-tier rule.
chunk_findings.title: tests/harness_conformance/gaps.json:86 (`parity_gaps`)

chunk_findings.detail: `parity_baseline()` raises `KeyError` when `gaps.json` exists as a JSON object but does not contain the new `parity_gaps` key. For example, an existing pre-change baseline such as `{"gaps": []}` (or a test fixture created with only the old `gaps` key) reaches `data["parity_gaps"]` and crashes. The function already treats a missing baseline file as an empty committed gap set, so a missing `parity_gaps` key in the same JSON shape should also yield `[]` (or fail with a clear ratchet error), not an unhandled exception. This breaks tests or upgrade paths that call `parity_baseline()` before the baseline has been rewritten by `report.py --write`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/harness_conformance/report.py:parity_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: `test_the_parity_gap_set_only_shrinks` is described as a ratchet test, but line 101 asserts `not known - now`, requiring the current gap set to equal the committed baseline. If a required row is answered and a parity gap is removed, `now` becomes a strict subset of `known`; the test fails with “stale parity gaps” even though the gap set only shrank. A ratchet that “only shrinks” should reject only new gaps (`now - known`), not legitimate shrinkage.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_parity_gate.py:101

chunk_findings.detail: `_print_phase_tasks` calls `view_list(c.repo, "task", phase=a.tasks)` without forwarding any of the list command’s pagination parameters (`limit`, `offset`, `all`) or any other query filters parsed from `a`. For example, if phase `P1` has more tasks than the viewer’s default page size, `ddflow phase list --tasks P1 --all` (or `--limit 5`) still returns the default-limited task set, and the non-JSON branch never emits the generic “showing X of Y” cut notice; the user sees a truncated list with no indication that rows were cut. This violates the stated requirement that pagination remain correct once `--tasks` is added.
